Fires on the word that closes off a phrase/clause — the final complement/object right before punctuation or end of statement ("all but **one**", "cmd + **c**", "yes I **would**,", "Update **Now**.", "fall on the **floor**…"); it is strongly suppressed on clause-continuing connectives and next-step verbs in procedural text ("and", "Shape", "scheduled").

L7·N2899unmasked layer
Fires on mid-phrase words (esp. "article", and prepositions/pronouns like "to", "from", "for", "it") inside self-referential phrases that point to a specific piece of text being presented ("posted **to** reddit", "the original … **article** published", "letter of appreciation **from**", "the rules **for** this challenge", "so here **it** is"); it is strongly *suppressed* at clause-closing punctuation, especially ".\n" or ")" right after an introductory "the following/below …" phrase.

This neuron appears to track lexical novelty/predictability: it fires on tokens that continue a fresh, non-repeated stretch of prose (e.g. "stay **at** home", "upon us **once** more", "is **one** of the most rewarding", "de**cept**ively", a name-initial at a document start), while it is strongly suppressed on tokens that are verbatim repeats of nearby text or boilerplate/list-entry boundaries (repeated "whirlpool", "Residential property owned by…", sentence-final ".\n" in repetitive citation/review lists).
